A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Tempora framework. All supplied pages, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison despite the substantial expansion in v2.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original accuracy, latency and temporal-utility experiments for seven TTA methods on ImageNet-C.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, controlled ablations, additional datasets, architectures and hardware experiments.

M1.justification: Tempora retains the same buffered discrete scheduler, hyperbolic delay discount and budget-exhaustion freezing procedure. Expanded simulation explanations and experimental variants do not establish a change to the proposed framework's core procedure.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates ImageNet-C only. Appendices C.7-C.8 in v2 add ImageNet-V2 natural distribution shifts, ImageNet-R artistic renditions and CIFAR-10-C corruptions, substantially broadening represented data and shift types while retaining image classification.

E2.justification: The ResNet-50 comparison expands from seven to nine TTA methods by adding DeYO and CMF. The new ViT comparisons additionally evaluate SPA and ZeroSIAM and exclude AdaBN because ViT uses layer normalisation. DeYO and SPA were cited but not evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: The original ResNet-50 settings remain, but v2 adds substantially different experimental configurations: ViT-B/16 with a 105.3 ms baseline and revised threshold/budget grids, and ResNet-18 CPU/GPU comparisons with budgets scaled to inference latency. The hardware comparison omits continuous evaluation; new buffering and normalisation controls also expand the evaluation design.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's pressure sweeps and utility decompositions, v2 directly compares buffered and unbuffered execution in Tables 8-9. Table 16 tests source-statistics retention and adaptation parameter scope using ETA and SHOT-IM variants. Hardware comparisons and expanded deficit profiles further investigate failure conditions.

E5.justification: Both versions already disclose single-seed experiments; v2 identifies seed 2025. It adds timing summaries with plus/minus entries in Table 9 and across-corruption standard deviations of rank correlations in Tables 25 and 45. These additions do not establish repeated-run uncertainty or significance testing.

E6.justification: With the enlarged ResNet-50 comparator set, offline winners change from ETA on all 15 corruptions to CMF on ten and DeYO on five; ETA's temporal wins change from 141/240 to 103/240 while its retained accuracy scores remain unchanged. v2 adds extensive results for the new configurations and ablations. Table 4 also replaces near-one covariance entries with near-zero values.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(3), the batch-index recurrence and the insolvency reasoning are retained. Renaming the served-index set from P to Q and explaining properties of the existing hyperbolic function do not introduce new mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The three-metric framework and central rank-instability thesis remain. v2 explicitly frames instability as persistence beyond earlier findings, foregrounds physical-time grounding and diagnostic decomposition as contributions, and states broader empirical generality. The abstract's ETA-specific headline is removed.

C2.justification: v1 speculates that SHOT-IM's objective explains its frozen accuracy; v2 attributes resilience to retained source running statistics, supported by Table 16. It also interprets contrasting batch- and layer-normalisation behaviour and adds substantive qualifications concerning hardware-specific rankings and default hyperparameters.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a direct code URL where v1 only referred to a supplementary repository, clarifies event-queue buffering and eviction, and identifies the Raspberry Pi 5 16 GB configuration. Core warmup, latency-calibration and frozen-BN implementation details were already present in v1.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix B substantially revise positioning by explicitly crediting Ghunaim et al. and Alfarra et al. with earlier rank-instability observations, then distinguishing Tempora through physical-time constraints and diagnostic decomposition. New method, architecture and dataset references accompany this expanded relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: The contribution block is reorganised from three empirical findings into framework scope, diagnosis and persistence. The temporal-pressure discussion and Discussion are substantially rewritten, Appendix B is reorganised, and Appendix C gains distinct architecture, dataset and hardware sections. These changes materially alter the narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3 incorporate additional methods, with expanded ranks and legends, and v2 adds the ViT rank plot in Figure 5. New ablation, deficit and hardware comparison tables introduce substantial display changes; winner tables gain offline columns, and a large ViT decomposition uses landscape orientation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical foundation and speculative explanation of frozen-model behaviour. Additional shifts, architectures and CPU hardware test applicability, while the buffering comparison and Table 16 ablation support protocol choices and a revised mechanism explanation. These gains outweigh presentation inconsistencies, notably Figure 5's 1-32 s budget labels conflicting with the 2.5-80 s grids in Tables 34 and 36. Single-seed and default-hyperparameter limitations remain.
